newsitem.title: ITALY: Priebke to stay under arrest pending new ruling.
newsitem.headline: Priebke to stay under arrest pending new ruling.

text.p: Italy's highest court on Thursday called for a constitutional ruling on whether former SS officer Erich Priebke was legitimately re-arrested after he was controversially freed by a war crimes trial in July.

Defence lawyer Velio di Rezze said the court of cassation's decision meant that the former German captain, accused of involvement in Italy's worst World War Two massacre, would have to remain in prison until the ruling.

"I can only express my anger because it is merely a means of delaying the question. Until the constitutional court makes its ruling, the court of cassation can make no decision on the appeal we made against Priebke's arrest," he said.
Di Rezze said he hoped the constitutional court would declare its position by the end of the month.
The 83-year-old Priebke was freed by a military tribunal in Rome in late July in a decision that was widely denounced and which sparked protests in Italy and abroad.

The tribunal found Priebke guilty of involvement in the 1944 massacre of 335 men and boys in Rome's Ardeatine Caves, but said it was unable to punish the former SS captain because the statute of limitations on the crime had run out.
The Ardeatine Caves massacre was a reprisal for a partisan attack on German troops.
Priebke was re-arrested hours after the tribunal released him and is now being held in a central Rome prison.

His lawyers had argued that the re-arrest was illegal on the grounds that the orders should have come from the judicial police rather than Justice Minister Giovanni Maria Flick and because it came before an extradition request.
They also said at the time of the re-arrest that the detention was illegal because Germany wanted to try Priebke for the same crimes for which he was tried in Italy.
Bonn has asked Italy to extradite Priebke and former SS major Karl Hass, who is currently under house arrest in Italy, to stand trial in Germany on war crimes charges.
Priebke and Hass have each admitted personally killing two of the victims at the Ardeatine Caves.
Italy has said Priebke cannot be extradited while appeals against the Italian case remained open.

Lawyers for relatives of the victims have appealed against the verdict, questioning the competence of the judges, while the prosecution has also appealed. The court of cassation is due to discuss the appeals next month.
Italy must also get permission from Argentina, where Priebke lived prior to his extradition, before they can hand him over to a third country. Argentina has barred his return.
